title: Separate quarter orbital fits remove at least 99.1 percent of test signal energy near a KIC 3230227 harmonic
abstract: We measure signal loss from two orbital subtraction models at Kepler release 25 sample times for KIC 3230227. Each model uses 40 orbital harmonics and a quadratic trend in each quarter. One model fits separate harmonic coefficients in each quarter. The other shares those coefficients across the mission. At the published weak-mode frequency 1.8441372 cycles per day, the separate-quarter model retains 0.093 to 0.094 of the input signal norm over all phases. The shared model retains 0.989 to 0.989. This is a deterministic sampling test. It does not find or reject a stellar mode. The result gives a frequency-dependent sensitivity check for searches near orbital harmonics. It does not model changes in binary light, detector response, or noise.

display.caption: Signal norm after orbital subtraction at the actual Kepler times. Shading covers all input phases. The dotted line marks a published weak-mode frequency. The residual spectra are descriptive and do not identify a mode.

citations.reason: The published weak-mode frequency and physical context define the test.
A residual search with separate-quarter orbital fits motivates a response test near the excluded harmonics.
A prior season-model test shows sensitivity to orbital harmonic order.
A joint fit separates close fixed frequencies rather than removing one before fitting the other.
